purpose: Independent practice of D2.1 — sorting events into 3 likelihood categories. Used as Lesson 2 consolidation artifact.
student_learning_goal: I can sort events into three likelihood groups.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can sort events into three likelihood groups.
header.character_watermark: Maybe Mae the Cat in the top-right corner with a clipboard. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.part_title: Part 1: Write I, P, or C.
parts.student_instructions: Read 6 events. Write I (impossible), P (possible), or C (certain) on the line.
parts.visual_layout: Six event rows stacked vertically, each with event text on the left and a small writing line on the right.

image_placeholders.description: Six event rows for a Grade 1 worksheet, B&W line art. Each row has an event sentence on the left (~4in) and a small writing line on the right (~1in). Events sample: 'Snow falls in July', 'Lunch will happen today', 'It might rain', 'A dragon walks into school', 'A friend smiles at me', 'My birthday is today'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P1_EVENTS at Part 1: instructions ask the child to label events as I, P, or C. Keywords name the three categories.

parts.answer_key: Snow in July: I. Lunch today: C. Might rain: P. Dragon: I. Friend smiles: P. Birthday: depends — accept any reasonable answer based on context.

parts.student_instructions: Sort the 9 events into the 3-column table.
parts.visual_layout: A 3-column sort table with 9 events listed below to sort.

image_placeholders.description: A 3-column sort table for a Grade 1 worksheet. Columns: IMPOSSIBLE, POSSIBLE, CERTAIN. Each column ~2in × 4in. Below the table, 9 short events listed in a numbered list (~0.4in each).
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P2_TABLE at Part 2: instructions ask the child to sort events. Keywords name the activity (sort) and the items (events).

parts.answer_key: Distribute 9 events appropriately into 3 columns (3 each).

parts.student_instructions: Make a TRICKY event for each likelihood. Tell why it fits.
parts.visual_layout: Three rows. Each row has a label, a writing line for the event, and a 'because' line for the reason.

image_placeholders.description: Three rows for a Grade 1 worksheet, B&W line art. Each row has the likelihood label on the left (IMPOSSIBLE / POSSIBLE / CERTAIN), a writing line for the event in the middle, and a separate 'because' line for the reason.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P3_TRICKY at Part 3: instructions ask the child to write a tricky event with a reason. Keywords name the prompt focus.

parts.answer_key: Any 3 events with valid 'because' reasons. Sample: 'IMPOSSIBLE: a pig flies because pigs cannot fly. POSSIBLE: rain because it sometimes rains. CERTAIN: lunch because it always happens.'

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, find an event in your day right now that's POSSIBLE.
teacher_notes: Lesson 2 consolidation artifact. Use Part 3 as the formative signal — children who provide valid 'because' reasons demonstrate deep understanding.
